card_summary: Given the emphasis on VFX breakdowns, signal integrity is paramount to maintain frame-accuracy. Architecturally, this implies a reliance on standards like ST 2110 for real-time transport and AES67 for audio over IP. In practice, this means engineering teams must carefully balance latency and signal quality, potentially leveraging JPEG XS for visually lossless compression. The trade-off here is between preserving signal fidelity and managing bandwidth, a challenge that requires careful planning and infrastructure design.

Why Real-Time Transport Is Forcing Broadcasters to Rethink Signal Integrity

Live signal transport is under pressure to deliver frame-accurate video and audio with minimal latency, and this shift is forcing broadcasters to rethink their architecture. As the demand for high-quality, low-latency live streaming continues to grow, broadcasters are being pushed to adopt new technologies that can meet these requirements.

What This Development Actually Means

The development of new live signal transport protocols such as ST 2110, NDI, and SRT is revolutionizing the way broadcasters approach real-time transport. These protocols offer improved signal integrity, reduced latency, and increased flexibility, making them ideal for live production and broadcast applications. For example, ST 2110 provides a standardized framework for IP-based media transport, while NDI offers a flexible and scalable solution for live video production.

The industry context for this development is the growing demand for live streaming and online video, which requires broadcasters to deliver high-quality, low-latency video and audio to a wide range of devices and platforms. This has created a need for new technologies that can meet these requirements, and the development of new live signal transport protocols is a response to this pressure.

Why It Matters for Broadcast Operations

The adoption of new live signal transport protocols such as ST 2110, NDI, and SRT will have significant implications for broadcast operations over the next 12-18 months. Broadcasters will need to assess the compatibility of their existing infrastructure with these new protocols and plan for upgrades or replacements as necessary. Vendors such as Matrox, Riedel, and Evertz are already developing products that support these new protocols, and broadcasters will need to evaluate these options carefully. For example, Matrox's ConvertIP gateway supports ST 2110 and can be used to convert SDI signals to IP, while Riedel's MediorNet platform offers a flexible and scalable solution for live video production.

Impact by Stakeholder

  • Regional and national broadcasters: Will need to budget for upgrades to their existing infrastructure to support new live signal transport protocols, which will reduce transmission costs and improve signal quality. They can eliminate the need for separate audio and video cables by using a single IP connection, simplifying signal routing and reducing hardware rack footprint.
  • OTT and streaming platforms: Will need to reassess their ABR ladder and CDN cost per GB to ensure they can deliver high-quality, low-latency video and audio to a wide range of devices and platforms. They will also need to consider the complexity of SSAI and the impact of latency on the user experience.
